market_summary: US and Asian markets show mixed signals as mega-cap tech faces headwinds and opportunities. Apple faces $5.7 billion patent judgment and advancing antitrust cases over App Store practices and tap-to-pay fees. Nvidia counters weakness with record $150bn buyback and new AI safety platform launch, supporting semiconductor stocks. Microsoft struggles with AI monetization concerns as adoption gaps widen globally. Tesla faces critical September 30 regulatory deadline on Cybercab safety certification. China signals potential easing of Nvidia chip restrictions for ByteDance and Alibaba. Singapore shares rose 0.3% on banking sector strength. Market focus remains on AI profitability, regulatory headwinds, and geopolitical trade tensions.

items.headline: Apple Ordered to Pay $5.7bn in Patent Infringement Case
items.summary: A California jury found Apple infringed two Taction Technology patents for haptic feedback technology used in iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple plans to appeal the verdict.

items.headline: Apple Pay Antitrust Lawsuit Advances as Class Certification Approved
items.summary: US District Judge Jeffrey White certified a class action lawsuit accusing Apple of blocking tap-to-pay competition, allowing banks and credit unions to sue together over Apple's NFC chip restrictions.

items.headline: Nvidia Launches AI Safety Platform and Announces Record $150bn Buyback
items.summary: Nvidia unveiled Open Agent Safety Platform to prevent AI agents from escaping controlled environments and announced $150bn stock buyback increase, raising total authorization to $235bn through fiscal 2028.

items.headline: Microsoft Stock Falls as AI Adoption Gap Reaches 12.6 Points Between Global North and South
items.summary: Microsoft reported global generative AI adoption at 18.8% of working-age people, but with a widening inequality gap of 12.6 percentage points between developed and developing regions, raising concerns about monetization.

items.headline: Tesla Must Answer NHTSA Questions on Cybercab Certification by September 30
items.summary: US regulators formally ordered Tesla to answer 21 questions by September 30, 2026 explaining how the steering-wheel-free Cybercab complies with federal safety standards. If rejected, Tesla could face a 2,500-unit annual production cap under Part 555 exemption.

items.headline: China Reportedly Weighs Allowing ByteDance and Alibaba to Purchase Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 Chips
items.summary: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has asked major domestic companies including ByteDance and Alibaba to submit procurement plans for Nvidia's RTX PRO 5500 chips and signaled intention to approve purchases.

items.headline: Singapore Shares End Higher as Bank Counters Rise
items.summary: Singapore's STI index rose 0.3% with bank stocks including UOB, DBS and OCBC outperforming the broader market.
